messages.subject: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
messages.subject_clean: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
messages.body_plain: I've recently finished a simulation where I generated many data sets with known, constant parameter values. I analyzed the simulated data with a method that estimates the data-generating parameters in JAGS. In addition to looking at things like bias, I recorded the proportion of BCIs that contained the true values.  Is this anything like coverage in classical inference?  Can a Bayesian use a frequentist view of probability in this way? BTW, in many simulations, nominal levels were not attained.  I attribute this result to non-asymptotic properties of the small data sets I analyzed, perhaps the use of poor (non-proper) priors, and the most obvious effect of parameter bias.  Any thoughts on this matter would be greatly appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
messages.subject_clean: A question about parameter estimation and coverage in a Bayesian inference framework
messages.body_plain:
Hi Brian,
There is no particular consensus on whether applying frequentist ideas to Bayesian model evaluation is "best practice" but a lot of people do it and I think it is useful for assessing whether a model is going to be useful in practice.  It can also be useful for rooting out pernicious bugs in your code...  But you're right, use of different priors (especially informative ones) make such assessments difficult to interpret at times.

 If you're interested in getting opinions of statisticians much better than myself, perhaps do a google search for 'calibrated Bayes.'

Cheers, Paul

messages.subject: open population multiple sites capture-recapture
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

Does anyone know an example of open-population capture-recapture study conducted in multiple sites?
I have capture histories of individuals for several sites and some sampled sites with no captures.
I'm specifically interested in modeling survival and entry probabilities with site covariates. I would like to, in some way, include the sites with no captures (possibly low entry probability).
I'm trying to figure out how to expand the POPAN/superpopulation formulation of Jolly-Seber to multiple sites.
Does it make sense?

Cheers,

Ismael V. Brack
PhD Student
Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul
Porto Alegre, Brazil

messages.subject: RE: Fitting CJS models with individual effects and truncated distributions
messages.subject_clean: Fitting CJS models with individual effects and truncated distributions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Blanca,

you're not doing anything wrong. It's just that JAGS doesn't allow this construct, since apparently it doesn't result in exactly the correct posterior distributions.

Perhaps you can try to reparameterize your model, e.g., like this, which may sometimes help:
for (t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
        logit(phi[i,t]) <- lphi[i,t]
        lphi[i,t] ~ dnorm(mu, tau)
}

Alternatively, you could use a slightly informative prior on sigma, e.g., a half-normal such as this:
sigma ~ dnorm(0, 1/3^2)I(0,)               # do this to see how it looks like: hist(abs(rnorm(10^6, 0, 3)))

In this latter case you could of course no longer say that you are using 'vague priors' but could call them 'weakly informative'. And it would be good to do a sensitivity analyses to see how much your estimates of sigma depend on your choice of prior.

Best regards  -- Marc

From: hmec...@googlegroups.com [hmec...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Blanca [blanc...@gmail.com]
Sent: 21 February 2020 11:53
To: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Subject: Fitting CJS models with individual effects and truncated distributions

Hello all,

I am trying to fit a CJS model with individual effect follow Kéry and Schaub book and I have convergence problems. I have read in Kéry and Royle, 2009 that this can be solved using a zero-mean truncated distribution. I have implemented it in JAGS, but it gives me an error. The code and the error showed below.

MODEL
sink("cjs_heter.jags")
cat("
    model {
    # Priors and constraints
    for (i in 1:nind){
      for (t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
        logit(phi[i,t]) <- mu + epsilon[i]
        p[i,t] <- mean.p
      }
    }
    for (i in 1:nind){
    epsilon[i] ~ dnorm(0,tau)I(-20,20)
    }

    # Priors
    mean.phi ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mu <- log(mean.phi / (1-mean.phi))
    sigma ~ dunif(0, 10)
    tau <- 1/(sigma*sigma)
    sigma2 <- pow(sigma, 2)
    mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)

    # Likelihood
    for (i in 1:nind){
    # Define latent state at first capture
    z[i,f[i]] <- 1
    for (t in (f[i]+1):n.occasions){
    # State process
    z[i,t] ~ dbern(mu1[i,t])
    mu1[i,t] <- phi[i,t-1] * z[i,t-1]
    # Observation process
    y[i,t] ~ dbern(mu2[i,t])
    mu2[i,t] <- p[i,t-1] * z[i,t]
    }
    }
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()

ERROR
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: RUNTIME ERROR:
Compilation error on line 11.
BUGS I(,) notation is only allowed if all parameters are fixed

Anyone could tell me what I am doing wrong?

Thanks in advance.

Blanca

messages.subject: Problem of 'possible directed cycle' in a dynamic site-occupancy model
messages.subject_clean: Problem of 'possible directed cycle' in a dynamic site-occupancy model
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm stuck in a problem of 'possible directed cycle' in a dynamic site-occupancy model using JAGS. The error appears when estimating Goodness-of-fit statistics following codes described in Chapter 15 of AHM2 book. We could expect a directed cycle when:
Example 1) using e.g. x[i] in both right and left side of a relation, and failing to specify some nodes, like:
for (i in 2:Nsamp) { x[i] ~ dnorm (0,1) } #, and then
y<- sum (x) # the directed cycle error will appear if we didn't specify x[1] as: x[1]<-0

Example 2) using x to specify y, using y to specify w, and using w to specify x, like this:
model {
   y[i]~dnorm (x[i],tau)
   w[i]~dnorm(y[i],tau)
   x[i]~dnorm (w[i],tau)
   tau <- dgamma(1,1)
}

In my case, the error "Possible directed cycle involving Chi2Open" appears when estimating the Chi-square discrepancy statistics for the open part of the dynamic model. The piece of code with error is:

# Computing Chi-square discrepancy
# tm is the transition matrix for observed data, and tmrep replicated data
## col1 in tm have the sum of noncolonized sites, and col2 the sum of colonized sites
## col2 in Etm have the sum of expected noncol sites, and col2 the sum of expected col sites.
## e is 0.0001

for (t in 1:(nweek-1)) {
      ## for observed data
       x2Open[1,1,t] <- pow((tm[1,1,t] - Etm[1,1,t]), 2) / (tm[1,1,t]+e)
       x2Open[1,2,t] <- pow((tm[1,2,t] - Etm[1,2,t]), 2) / (tm[1,2,t]+e)
       x2Open[2,1,t] <- pow((tm[2,1,t] - Etm[2,1,t]), 2) / (tm[2,1,t]+e)
       x2Open[2,2,t] <- pow((tm[2,2,t] - Etm[2,2,t]), 2) / (tm[2,2,t]+e)
       # ... for replicated data
       x2repOpen[1,1,t] <- pow((tmrep[1,1,t]-Etm[1,1,t]),2)/(tmrep[1,1,t]+e)
       x2repOpen[1,2,t] <- pow((tmrep[1,2,t]-Etm[1,2,t]),2)/(tmrep[1,2,t]+e)
       x2repOpen[2,1,t] <- pow((tmrep[2,1,t]-Etm[2,1,t]),2)/(tmrep[2,1,t]+e)
       x2repOpen[2,2,t] <- pow((tmrep[2,2,t]-Etm[2,2,t]),2)/(tmrep[2,2,t]+e)
    }
    # Add up overall test statistic and compute fit stat ratio (open part)
    Chi2Open <- sum(x2Open[,,]) # Chisq. statistic for observed data
    Chi2repOpen <- sum(x2repOpen[,,]) # Chisq. statistic for replicated data
    Chi2ratioOpen <- Chi2Open / Chi2repOpen ## Ratio between obs and rep data

I was wondering if some nodes of 'x2Open' remained undefined (like Example 1), since I couldn't easily find the directed cycle like Example 2 in the beginning of the message. Furthermore, if I try only "Chi2Open", JAGS reports the following error: "Cannot evaluate subset expression for Chi2Open" -- perhaps meaning that some nodes didn't exist.

Any help with that?

Thanks a ton.

André Luza

PS: I didn't send the complete code because AHM2 has not yet been published.
--

André Luís Luza

Post-Doc Researcher
Programa de Pós-Graduação em Ecologia
Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul
Porto Alegre- BR
